neighbours.label: the slot right before a belief/expectation verb: 'led to [believe]', 'reason to [suspect]', French 'laisser [présager/penser]'
fire: For years the public was led to believe the bridge was perfectly safe.
Investors had every reason to suspect the figures were inflated.
Nothing in his early films would have led anyone to expect such a hit.
The surgeon said there was good reason to suspect a hidden infection.
We were led to believe that the shipment had already left the port.
Rien dans ses premiers romans ne laissait présager un tel succès.
The quiet morning gave no reason to think a storm was coming.
Her calm tone led the staff to assume nothing was wrong.
quiet: For years the public was led to the bridge by a narrow path.
Investors had every reason to celebrate the strong figures.
Nothing in his early films would have led anyone to the studio.
The surgeon said there was good reason to operate on the knee.
We were led to the dock where the shipment had already left.
Rien dans ses premiers romans ne parlait de la guerre ou de Paris.
The quiet morning gave us time to walk before the storm.
Her calm tone led the staff to the meeting room on time.
